{"artifact":"SmeDossierEnvelope","schema_version":"0.4.0","stage_id":"02.dossier_sections","probe":"rdmv-wi-d","lineage":{"input_manifest_sha256":"21fc4d6267d14ff4797cbacd342eab4353f8722c44c9de2aeb049879c4472506","candidate_lineage_id":"2026-10-28-rdmv-wi-class-d:lineage:15","source_registry_sha256":"9dcfc0d0c3044debd01d4cb03103f48fb860797364a23b2cb56d36c868619a64","source_liveness_sha256":"4ca51030ff51b3372629ada1c05ad91f501dabccdcf7931dab678c717e7bb9b6"},"envelope_scope":{"kind":"partial_chunk","assigned_section_ids":["C2"],"chunk_index":1,"chunk_total":1},"section_char_limit":12000,"sections":[{"section_id":"C2","chunk_id":"C2.01","merge_seq":1,"domain":"Maneuver confusables: U-turn versus Y-turn, hill wheel positions, low versus high beams and signal timing","heading":"C2 — Confusable pairs and knowledge-graph hints: U-turn versus Y-turn, the three hill-parking cases, passing rules, low versus high beams, and signal timing before versus after an intersection","learner_facing":false,"markdown":"## C2 — Confusable pairs and knowledge-graph hints: U-turn versus Y-turn, the three hill-parking cases, passing rules, low versus high beams, and signal timing before versus after an intersection
Confusable pairs among turning, passing, parking and signaling rules, where look-alike maneuvers and mirror-image wheel positions are easy to mix up; each block ties to one handbook page, and hint metadata sits only in the trailing line of a block.

FACT_ID: sec04-R01 | anchor: A01
Large trucks and buses may swing across the center line while turning, but you must not cross it yourself, so give them extra room instead. [A01]
Why it matters: group turning; confusable large vehicle versus car turning path.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0018]

FACT_ID: sec04-R02 | anchor: A02
A U-turn is a single continuous motion and is allowed on any rural two-lane highway when safe, unless a sign forbids it. [A02]
Why it matters: group turnarounds; confusable U-turn versus Y-turn; prereq sign reading.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0019]

FACT_ID: sec04-R03 | anchor: A04
A Y-turn is a stop-and-reverse turnaround reserved for residential streets too narrow for a U-turn, and it is also a graded maneuver on the driving exam. [A04]
Why it matters: group turnarounds; confusable Y-turn versus U-turn.
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0021]

FACT_ID: sec04-R04 | anchor: A04
In the Y-turn the only reversing step is the third one, where you look back over your right shoulder before backing. [A04]
Why it matters: group turnarounds; difficulty medium.
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0021]

FACT_ID: sec04-R05 | anchor: A04
Passing on the left is the normal pass, while going around on a paved shoulder is allowed only past a stopped or left-turning vehicle. [A04]
Why it matters: group passing; confusable left-lane pass versus shoulder.
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0021]

FACT_ID: sec04-R06 | anchor: A04
Checking mirrors is not enough before a lane change, because the blind spots are seen only by looking over the shoulder toward the new lane. [A04]
Why it matters: group lane changes; misconception mirrors are enough.
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0021]

FACT_ID: sec04-R07 | anchor: A05
After passing, the cue that it is safe to move back into the driving lane is seeing both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror. [A05]
Why it matters: group passing; misconception return as soon as alongside.
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0022]

FACT_ID: sec04-R08 | anchor: A05
The speed limit still applies while passing, and the vehicle being passed has no duty to move over for you. [A05]
Why it matters: group passing; misconception passing allows speeding.
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0022]

FACT_ID: sec04-R09 | anchor: A05
A missed exit is handled by driving to the next exit and coming back, never by backing up on the road. [A05]
Why it matters: group backing; misconception backing to a missed exit.
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0022]

FACT_ID: sec04-R10 | anchor: A06
Uphill with a curb is the left-wheel case, while uphill without a curb and every downhill park are right-wheel cases. [A06]
Why it matters: group hill parking; confusable curb versus no curb.
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0023]

FACT_ID: sec04-R11 | anchor: A06
When you begin parallel parking you stop about 2 feet from the car ahead, and the space you choose should be about 3-6 feet longer than your car. [A06]
Why it matters: group parallel parking; confusable gap beside versus space length.
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0023]

FACT_ID: sec04-R12 | anchor: A07
At the end of a parallel park you should be about a foot from the curb, but at least 2 feet from the vehicles ahead and behind. [A07]
Why it matters: group parallel parking; confusable curb distance versus vehicle distance.
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0024]

FACT_ID: sec04-R13 | anchor: A07
A light tap on the horn is for getting attention, while a hard press is reserved for warning of an imminent collision. [A07]
Why it matters: group communication; confusable tap versus hard press.
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0024]

FACT_ID: sec04-R14 | anchor: A08
Low beams are required at the 500-foot visibility threshold and in the half hour after sunset through the half hour before sunrise, but are only recommended with wipers on or in rain, snow or fog. [A08]
Why it matters: group lights; confusable required versus recommended.
Source: [A08 -> pdf-0025]

FACT_ID: sec04-R15 | anchor: A08
High beams double your seeing distance compared with low beams, yet must be dimmed when a vehicle approaches; parking lights are only for when you are parked and idling. [A08]
Why it matters: group lights; confusable high beams versus parking lights.
Source: [A08 -> pdf-0025]

FACT_ID: sec04-R16 | anchor: A08
At an intersection you signal about three seconds, roughly 100 feet, ahead of the turn, but for a turn just past an intersection you wait until you have crossed it. [A08]
Why it matters: group signals; confusable before versus after an intersection.
Source: [A08 -> pdf-0025]

FACT_ID: sec04-R17 | anchor: A08
In hand signals a straight arm means a left turn, an arm bent upward means a right turn, and an arm pointed down means slowing or stopping. [A08]
Why it matters: group signals; confusable left versus right hand signal.
Source: [A08 -> pdf-0025]
